title: Introduction, Variables, and Data Types
objectives: Explain the purpose of JavaScript.
Declare variables using let and const.
Identify common JavaScript data types.
Use typeof to inspect values.
introduction: Learn JavaScript uses; HTML/CSS/JS; script tags and external files; let/const/var; names and reassignment; strings, numbers, booleans, null, undefined, arrays, objects; typeof and conversion. Practice the example, then write your own activity.
explanation: JavaScript adds behavior to web pages: HTML provides structure and CSS provides presentation. In a normal page, use <script src="main.js" defer></script> to load an external script after parsing; this lab loads its JavaScript editor separately in an interpreter. Prefer const for bindings you do not reassign and let when reassignment is needed. var is function-scoped and has older hoisting behavior. Names are case-sensitive identifiers and cannot be reserved words. Arrays store ordered values; objects group named properties. typeof gives type information, with historical exceptions: typeof null is "object" and arrays also report "object"; use Array.isArray for arrays. Number(text) converts numeric text; validate conversion before calculation.

loadStudents();

introduction: Learn localStorage/sessionStorage; JSON storage; privacy; XSS; safe text; secrets; least privilege; lab isolation. Practice the example, then write your own activity.
explanation: Real localStorage stores origin-scoped strings across browser sessions; sessionStorage has a shorter tab-session lifetime. Store JSON text when suitable, but validate restored values and handle unavailable/quota-limited storage. Neither is secure storage for passwords or tokens against scripts running in the same origin. XSS happens when attacker-controlled text becomes executable markup or script. Prefer textContent and explicit validation. This lab provides temporary virtual storage, reset on Run, with no access to real site cookies or storage; localStorage and sessionStorage use the same practice store here. Production security belongs in the application and server as well as the frontend.
